name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz flows ~54% of prewar; Red Sea attacks
summary: Hormuz oil flows about 54% of prewar in the week to 24 Nov; Iran's Guards report another tanker hit on 27 Nov
state: Kpler data show crude clearing Hormuz averaged 9.25m barrels a day in the seven days to 24 Nov, about 54% of the prewar 17.1m (The National). UKMTO reported a projectile striking a tanker transiting the strait on 26 Nov (BOE Report), and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said another tanker was hit in Hormuz on 27 Nov (Al Jazeera). Houthi attacks on Saudi Red Sea ports continue, so two chokepoints remain disrupted.
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf and Red Sea faces attack risk, longer routes and higher insurance costs, which feed into fuel and freight prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state advisories.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (~54% of prewar) and Red Sea disrupted = Alert

sources.title: The National — Oil set to post weekly gain as Middle East attacks stoke supply concerns
BOE Report — Tanker struck by projectile while transiting Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
Al Jazeera — Iran war live: IRGC says tanker hit in Hormuz; Araghchi calls deadly Kuwait attack suspicious

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
